Website: https://bb0928.github.io/forge/.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: EG360: Efficient and Generalizable $360^\circ$ Depth Estimation via Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation and Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Laiyan Ding, Chongxi Meng, Rui Huang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: EG360 introduces an efficient panorama depth estimation model that achieves robust zero-shot generalization with only 6.593M parameters, enabling real-time performance on embedded platforms.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Generalized panorama depth estimation has witnessed great advances in recent years. These methods typically achieve robust zero-shot generalization performance using large pretrained models, but their high computational cost makes real-time inference on embedded platforms challenging. In contrast, previous lightweight panorama models have mostly been developed for single-domain evaluations and cannot generalize well due to domain shifts. To reduce the gap between these two types of models, we introduce EG360, an efficient and generalizable panorama depth estimation model. Specifically, building on a lightweight depth model, we design an Adaptive Panorama-Perspective Distillation (APPD) strategy guided by scene geometry, along with a Spherical Cross-Level Feature Fusion (SCFF) module for global semantic perception. As a result, with only 6.593M parameters after reparameterization, EG360 achieves strong zero-shot performance on real-world benchmarks and runs at 35 FPS on a Jetson Orin NX 16GB in MAXN mode, whereas a previous ViT-small model runs at less than 2 FPS. Our code will also be made public for future research.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: I See What You Want: Decoding Hierarchical Operator Intent from Visual Teleoperation History
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Xiangyi Jia, Kaixian Qu, Shengzhi Wang, Chenyu Yang, Robert Katzschmann
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The paper introduces VI AMO, a dataset for hierarchical intent prediction in teleoperation, and demonstrates that fine-tuning a vision-language model significantly improves action and mission decoding, enhancing robotic autonomy.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have become a powerful foundation for robotic scene understanding, task planning, and language-conditioned control. A natural question follows: can these models also decode what a human operator intends while teleoperating a robot, without any explicit instruction? We formulate this as hierarchical intent prediction, jointly inferring the ongoing atomic action and the broader mission it serves from a short visual teleoperation history. To study this, we introduce VI AMO (Vision Intention Action and Mission Ongoing), a dataset of 6,600 episodes from eleven robot sources with 13,653 temporally aligned action annotations and 9,702 mission annotations. Large proprietary models struggle with this problem: on held-out episodes, GPT-4o reaches Sentence-BERT similarities of only 0.563 and 0.470 for action and mission, and GPT-5.6 Luna achieves only 0.581 and 0.554. Fine-tuning a VLM on VI AMO yields our Vision-Intention Model (VIM), which raises these scores to 0.825 and 0.821 and still reaches 0.726 and 0.717 on the 35.4% of test actions with both labels absent from training. Finally, as a downstream application, VIM's predicted mission enables a vision-language-action (VLA) policy to take over from the operator mid-task in a real-world environment unseen during VIM fine-tuning, reducing human teleoperation time by 34.6% relative to GPT-4o and 39.8% relative to GPT-5.6 Luna, while cutting intent-prediction latency by roughly 70% on average.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: BWM-Forge: Agentic World Programming for Embodied Intelligence
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: BWM-Forge is a code-driven framework enabling controllable video generation for robotics by constructing editable Blender scenes from various inputs, enhancing aesthetic and motion quality across tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Generating diverse robot videos requires control over scene geometry, robot motion, and viewpoints. End-to-end video generation offers limited direct access to these variables, making targeted edits and reuse across tasks difficult. We present BWM-Forge, a code-driven framework for controllable video generation in robotics. Given robot assets and a task description, the framework accepts an initial image, an image with motion data, or a human demonstration video. A coding agent constructs editable Blender scene programs that specify objects, robot motion, and cameras. The resulting proxy videos provide structural and motion references for a video generation model, which adds visual detail. A multi-agent harness coordinates input processing, scene construction, review, and rendering. Automated evaluation and user feedback support iterative refinement, while an experience repository stores and retrieves reusable modeling and rendering rules. This design supports multiple robot embodiments, synchronized viewpoints, and appearance variation from a shared scene program. We evaluate the framework on 15 tasks covering five robot types. Compared with LingBot-World Base Cam on these tasks, BWM-Forge achieves higher aesthetic quality, imaging quality, subject and background consistency, motion smoothness, and RoboJudge-9B physical adherence and instruction alignment scores. The baseline scores higher in dynamic degree. Qualitative cases illustrate viewpoint control, scene variation, feedback-driven edits, and experience reuse across scenes. These results demonstrate a practical approach to generating controllable robot videos through editable, executable scene representations.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: HAVANA: A Hierarchical Video-Action Model for Vision-Language Navigation
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Dongzhihan Wang, Yi Du, Chen Wang, Xiuxian Li, Liang Xu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: HAVANA introduces a dual-system video-action model for Vision-Language Navigation that separates predictive reasoning from local planning, enhancing navigation performance and generalization in diverse environments.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires long-horizon instruction-consistent planning and short-horizon path planning grounded in the currently observed geometry. Anticipating how future observations evolve along the instructed route provides predictive guidance beyond the current field of view, motivating video-action models (VAMs) that learn representations of future visual states. However, many existing VAMs couple future visual prediction with action generation during inference, despite their distinct temporal requirements: instruction-conditioned route guidance can be reused across multiple control steps, whereas local trajectories must continuously adapt to fresh observations. To bridge this gap, we introduce HAVANA, a dual-system VAM that decouples predictive reasoning from reactive local planning. A slow system produces a compact language-conditioned latent plan from observation history, while a fast system combines the latest plan with the current observation to generate local trajectories. Their asynchronous execution enables rapid adaptation without repeated future prediction, and no future video is generated during inference. Experiments on OmniNavBench demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance over prior baselines, while zero-shot real-world deployments further show robust generalization to unseen environments.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: AgroOmni: A Large-Scale Multi-view Agricultural Dataset for Cross-Scale Multimodal Reasoning
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Jiarui Zhang, Junqi Hu, Zurong Mai, Yang Liu, Yuhang Chen
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: AgroOmni is a comprehensive multi-view agricultural dataset that enhances multimodal reasoning and cross-scale understanding, significantly improving performance in agricultural perception tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: Modern agricultural data is sourced from diverse platforms and spans multiple spatial scales, ranging from ground-level close-up photography to Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) aerial observation and satellite remote sensing imagery. Accordingly, agricultural multimodal reasoning demands robust cross-scale spatial understanding. However, due to the lack of multi-view agricultural benchmark datasets, existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs) exhibit severe ground-level bias, which leads to scale confusion then semantic collapse in agricultural perception tasks, such as misinterpreting farmland imagery as walls or floors. To address this, we introduce AgroOmni, a large-scale multi-view training corpus with 268,119 Visual Question Answering pairs covering 56 specialized task categories across 14 task types, designed to capture diverse scales in modern precision agriculture.Built on this dataset, we propose AgroNVILA, which achieves a new state-of-the-art of 59.86% on the AgroMind benchmark (+12.57 over GPT-5.2), effectively mitigating the multi-view cross-scale gap for holistic agricultural understanding. Diagnostic evaluations on AgMMU further reveal an inherent heterogeneity between macro-priors and micro-diagnostics through constrained zero-shot performance. Meanwhile, even minimal fine-tuning leads to a dramatic performance gain of AgroNVILA on AgMMU, strongly demonstrating its generalization capability empowered by AgroOmni. Full training scripts are publicly available at https://github.com/Jrookie2005/AgroOmni, and the AgroOmni dataset is released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/AgroOmni/AgroOmni.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Bind-WAM: Binding-Uncertainty-Guided Selective Future Imagination in World Action Models
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Chenhao Qiu, Shuyi Chen, Songen Gu, Shufeng Nan, Tianyu Wang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: Bind-WAM enhances robot learning by selectively invoking future imagination based on binding uncertainty, improving efficiency in predicting actions and visual states during task execution.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) can improve robot learning by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, but generating a visual future at every replanning step is expensive and sometimes unnecessary. This raises a critical question: when should a robot policy imagine the future? In this paper, we propose Bind-WAM, a binding-uncertainty-guided WAM for selective future imagination. Bind-WAM introduces language-object binding uncertainty, selectively invoking joint future-action generation when the current observation does not support stable task-relevant action generation. An offline labeling pipeline uses complete demonstrations and action context to identify task-relevant objects and detect reference mismatch, invisibility, and identity drift. The resulting pseudo-labels supervise a lightweight router that predicts binding uncertainty from the current observation and language instruction. At inference, a shared WAM policy invokes selective future imagination according to the predicted uncertainty and its change between consecutive replanning steps. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate that Bind-WAM can establish binding uncertainty as a strong, interpretable signal for selective future imagination.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: AFTER: A World Model with Adaptive Fast--Slow Timescales for Error-Driven Retention
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Haoyi Zhang, Qi Zhang, Yunfan Ren, Yi Bin, Lei Zhu
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: AFTER-WM introduces a world model that adapts to sudden changes in robot dynamics using adaptive fast-slow timescales for improved responsiveness, stability, and persistence in predictions.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: In robotics and embodied AI, a core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics during interaction. For instance, when a robotic arm grasps an object with an unknown payload, the robot dynamics change suddenly. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to simultaneously satisfy three critical requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, reacting promptly to sudden changes to curb prediction error accumulation; stability, distinguishing persistent changes from transient disturbances to prevent incorrect updates; and persistence, retaining the adapted dynamics without new observations so that later predictions do not revert to the old dynamics. Inspired by predictive coding in the human brain with multi-timescale adaptation, we propose AFTER-WM, a world model with Adaptive Fast-slow Timescales for Error-driven Retention, whose prediction errors drive a fast correction that fades and a slow correction that persists, while dynamically adjusting the combination weights of pre-trained experts without altering them, to overcome the trade-offs among responsiveness, stability and persistence. On five simulated robot datasets and real UAV data, AFTER-WM has a lower multi-step mean error than all ten compared models and the highest mean return in a joint-failure control task. In simulation, its multistep mean error is 16%-34% below the strongest compared model's and is also the lowest 1-4 steps after a change and under transient disturbances alone, and its step-40 error is the lowest as well, reflecting responsiveness, stability and persistence. All code (method, baselines, experiments) and datasets will be released online.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: Elastra: A Simulation Framework for Elastic Bodies
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Youran Sun, Chugang Yi, Xingyu Ren, Haizhao Yang
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: Elastra is a simulation framework for modeling robot interactions with elastic surfaces, enhancing control policies through reinforcement learning, significantly improving success rates in dynamic environments.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: When robots interact with elastic surfaces such as mattresses and trampolines, changes in loading cause the surfaces to deform and rebound, altering subsequent contact locations and forces. We present Elastra, a simulation framework for modeling this interaction and supporting the training and evaluation of robot control policies. Elastra represents each surface using elements that move only vertically, with elastic connections and damping to model deformation and recovery. Contact forces drive surface motion, and the updated surface geometry is used to compute subsequent contact forces. We systematically validate our simulations against an independent implementation and a real mattress load curve. We further use Elastra to train the Unitree G1 humanoid to stand up on mattresses and trampolines. Using the pretrained HoST policy and ProtoMotions motion tracker as original controllers, we train residual policies through reinforcement learning to add corrections to their joint targets. Adding these residual policies increases the success rate with HoST from 44.1\% to 72.5\%, and from 55\% to 89\% on the trampoline. With ProtoMotions, the success rate increases from 19.0\% to 45.0\% for initial poses not encountered during training. The code and video are available on https://github.com/yichg/elastra.

机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).authors_text: Yu Zhou, Xinyuan Xia, Xuankun Yang, Yinghao Yang, Wendi Chen
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).summary: The paper presents SWAM, a model that enhances language-video-action alignment through extensive video datasets and training strategies, achieving superior generalization in robotic tasks.
机器人与人工智能实验室 (RAIL).debug_abstract: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. Existing studies focus primarily on architectures and training mechanisms, typically treating language-video alignment acquired through video pretraining as an established foundation. However, introducing action learning may impair this alignment. Principled guidance on data and supervision design for maintaining language-video alignment during action learning remains limited. To investigate this, we curate a pool of approximately 47,000 hours of general videos, egocentric videos, UMI demonstrations, and robot demonstrations. Building on this, we systematically study how language-video supervision, language-video-action supervision, and the joint use of these two forms affect WAM performance. In particular, we examine how language annotation quality affects pretrained language-video capabilities, and how action supervision from UMI and robot demonstrations extends these capabilities to language-video-action modeling. To better scale the model, we further conduct detailed studies on joint training recipe and model architecture. Under a fixed training budget, mixing egocentric videos and UMI demonstrations improves control generalization. Model architecture affects how effectively these experiences are used, while scaling pretraining under the selected configuration brings further gains. The resulting recipe, post-trained on RoboTwin Clean demonstrations only, achieves success rates of 88.10% and 61.56% under Easy (Clean-to-Clean) and Hard (Clean-to-Random) conditions, respectively. Our model achieves 40.00% SR across three real-world tasks, compared with 23.33% for the strongest baseline, indicating better generalization under unseen conditions. We release the curated data, training code, and model weights.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Towards Robust Vision-Language Reasoning: A Multi-Stage Optimization Pipeline with Masked Diffusion Model
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Shunming Liu, Pei Huang, Yajing Sun, Huaxiao Liu
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: The paper presents a multi-stage optimization pipeline for enhancing vision-language reasoning in autonomous driving using a Masked Diffusion Model, achieving significant performance improvements over traditional methods.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Discrete diffusion generation is emerging as a competitive alternative to autoregressive generation by denoising the entire token sequence through iterative refinement. Its global planning and progressive correction capabilities are particularly well suited to autonomous driving. However, transferring this generation paradigm from general-purpose settings to driving introduces substantial domain gaps in both training and inference. To unlock its potential, we propose a multi-stage optimization pipeline for standard vision-language model architectures, without auxiliary action experts or specialized mixture-of-experts Transformer, spanning post-training and inference. During supervised fine-tuning, we optimize the representation of planning inputs to suppress hallucinations in task responses. During reinforcement learning, we introduce metric-guided diversity filtering to identify stronger learning starting points and improve policy exploration. At inference time, we propose Dynamic Autonomous Driving Decoding (DAD), which adaptively adjusts decoding modes according to scene complexity. Based on this pipeline, we develop Masked Diffusion Drive (MD-Drive), improving its performance by 29.7\% over the unoptimized model. Experiments on the NAVSIM closed loop benchmark and the nuScenes and DriveCoT open loop datasets show that MD-Drive outperforms autoregressive VLM baselines with the same architecture, while achieving a more favorable balance between performance and computational cost than systems with different architectures through discrete diffusion training and inference.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Can MLLMs Reason over Surround-View Driving Videos? A Multi-View Autonomous Driving QA Benchmark
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Shunming Liu, Jianyi Peng, Cheng Li, Lu Hou, Pei Huang
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: The paper introduces MVDriveBench, a benchmark evaluating MLLMs' spatio-temporal reasoning in autonomous driving using surround-view videos, revealing current limitations in their capabilities.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Surround-view video understanding in autonomous driving is a crucial capability for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to achieve reliable driving reasoning. Real-world driving often requires information beyond the front-view camera. Existing MLLMs primarily focus on front-view information, while their spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning abilities remain unknown. To address this gap, we propose MVDriveBench, a high-information-density video QA benchmark for autonomous driving, characterized by synchronized surround-view inputs, spatio-temporal understanding, and reasoning-chain-oriented evaluation. We design 12 categories of QA tasks that cover the complete reasoning pipeline from low-level visual perception to high-level driving decision-making, enabling a systematic evaluation of MLLMs surround-view spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning capabilities in complex driving environments. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 23 open-source, closed-source, and expert MLLMs on MVDriveBench. The results show that current MLLMs still exhibit insufficient surround-view spatio-temporal reasoning ability. Meanwhile, closed-loop evaluations of specialist models in AlpaSim reveal a correlation between surround-view spatio-temporal reasoning capabilities and closed-loop driving performance, highlighting the importance of comprehensive multi-view understanding for reliable vehicle control.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Remember What Changes the Odds: Critic-Gated Event Memory for Long-Horizon Manipulation
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Xuanzhuo Liu, Chuankang Li, Maoqing Yao, Guanghui Ren
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: The paper introduces CGEM, a critic-gated event memory that enhances long-horizon manipulation by selectively retaining events that significantly alter success probabilities, achieving 88% success in complex tasks.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: In long-horizon manipulation, a robot may need to take different actions under identical observations, depending on task progress and the outcomes of earlier attempts. We refer to this ambiguity as decision aliasing. Resolving it requires the policy to maintain memory of its execution history. To reduce the cost of processing full observation histories, recent methods build compact event memories using perceptual, semantic, or kinematic cues. However, these criteria may miss events that matter for task success. We instead propose an outcome-grounded principle: remember events that substantially change the predicted probability of eventual success. Following this principle, we introduce CGEM, a critic-gated event memory that uses a critic to select events with large estimated changes in success probability. Positive and negative changes are encoded as progress and failure records, respectively. Failure records are discarded once the corresponding subtask is completed. In a ten-subtask diagnostic environment with exactly computed success probabilities, CGEM achieves 88.0% success, compared with 0.0% for both a 36-step observation window and a kinematic event memory. Removing failure records reduces success to 1.7%.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Haoran Luo, Shangkai Lin, Jinyang Wu, Xinliang Zhou, Luu Anh Tuan
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: HyperSkill introduces a training-free framework utilizing a hypergraph-indexed skill library to enhance reinforcement learning performance across multiple modalities without updating model parameters.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning sharpens LLM reasoning, but parameter updates are expensive, forgetful, and opaque; training-free libraries swap gradients for a textual store but still use trajectory-level, correlation-based admission and flat structure. To address both, we propose HyperSkill, a Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO framework that keeps the backbone frozen and replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library, where skills are advantage-bearing nodes and compositions are hyperedges. It has three components: training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them; and an execution protocol makes the frozen backbone commit to an answer. On 11 text, vision-language, and omnimodal benchmarks, HyperSkill is best or tied on every dataset and beats the best baseline by 13.0 average F1 points while keeping the backbone frozen. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/LHRLAB/HyperSkill.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Back to the Question: Tracing Visual Distraction Through Text Tokens
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Marie Amale Huynh, Regev Cohen, Serena Yeung-Levy, Sivan Doveh
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: This paper analyzes the impact of visual distractors on vision-language models, revealing interference mechanisms and proposing answer consistency regularization to enhance accuracy despite distractions.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: The visual world is cluttered: robust vision-language reasoning requires ignoring irrelevant information. Yet vision-language models (VLMs) can suffer substantial accuracy losses when answering questions about a target image with distractors present. Existing mitigations focus on selecting relevant images or limiting information exchange between images. Through a systematic analysis of three open 7-8B VLMs on five perception benchmarks adapted to include distractor images, we show that distractors reduce accuracy even when models correctly identify the relevant image, suggesting that selection alone is not enough. To understand the mechanism behind this interference, we combine attention analysis with targeted knockouts in Qwen2.5-VL and identify middle-layer distractor-to-text connections as a pathway through which irrelevant visual information affects reasoning. We introduce answer consistency regularization, which encourages consistent answer distributions with and without distractors. Without directly constraining attention, this objective reduces middle-layer attention from question tokens to distractor images, consistent with the pathway our analysis implicates. With five distractors, our approach improves circular accuracy by an average of 16 percentage points over the Qwen2.5-VL baseline across the five benchmarks while preserving single-image performance.

斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).authors_text: Eve Fleisig, Joachim Baumann, Dylan Hadfield-Menell, Dirk Hovy
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).summary: The paper reveals that preference-based model evaluations, particularly in arena-style rankings, are susceptible to manipulation through strategic voting, prompting, and nomination, significantly distorting model rankings.
斯坦福-视觉与学习实验室 (SVL).debug_abstract: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models). We demonstrate these effects on public leaderboard data, analyze the circumstances that cause these vulnerabilities, and describe approaches to safeguard against each attack. Notably, these issues hold for any preference-based evaluation using the Bradley-Terry model that allows open prompting, voting, or model submission. These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have made significant progress in general-purpose robotic manipulation. Synteraction Lab.title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation
Synteraction Lab.authors_text: Quang Qui-Vinh Nguyen, Hung Nguyen, Rang Nguyen, Khoi Nguyen

Matched simulation studies and hardware experiments further show that ILA improves responsiveness to human guidance while preserving nominal motion-tracking performance. These results demonstrate compliant guidance as a reusable, sensor-free extension to pretrained humanoid motion trackers.

Microsystem Engineering and Robotics.title: Rethinking "RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes": The Role of SFT Data
Microsystem Engineering and Robotics.authors_text: Yunlong Hou, Fengzhuo Zhang, Yuan Cheng, Jiachun Pan, Xingyao Li
Microsystem Engineering and Robotics.summary: This paper argues that carefully curated and scaled Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) datasets can enhance generalization in language models, potentially surpassing Reinforcement Learning (RL) methods.
Microsystem Engineering and Robotics.debug_abstract: Large language models trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) with verifiable rewards exhibit strong reasoning ability and broad generalization, whereas models trained with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) are often viewed as more prone to memorization and limited transfer. This paper rethinks this distinction through the lens of SFT training data on widely used Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 series models. First, we study the role of data source and show that it is critical: a carefully mixed SFT dataset substantially outperforms data generated solely by a larger model. Second, we study the role of data scale and show that matching the number of correct rollouts between SFT and RL greatly improves SFT generalization, while matching the total rollout budget enables SFT to generalize as well as RL. Combining these two factors further enables SFT to generalize even better than RL. Third, by using LLM annotations to characterize the solution methods in training rollouts, we show that larger datasets cover more tail methods and that these tail methods provide generalizable reasoning signals. Finally, we support these empirical findings theoretically by analyzing the training dynamics of shallow transformers under both RL and SFT.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Donglin Yang, Xiangyu Wang, Yantong Zhong, Wenhao Zheng, Zihan Ding
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: UAV-Flow++ introduces a benchmark and learning framework for language-guided UAV navigation, enhancing short-range maneuvers through a comprehensive dataset and advanced training methods.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Language-guided UAV navigation has largely focused on long-horizon route planning, leaving short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers underexplored. To address this gap, we formulate Flying-on-a-Word (Flow), a task requiring a UAV to convert concise natural-language instruction, egocentric visual observation, and current state dynamics into continuous flight actions. Flow encompasses both primitive motion commands and complex object-interactive behaviors, assessing motion intent comprehension and spatial context grounding. To enable policy learning and closed-loop evaluation, we introduce UAV-Flow, a comprehensive dataset comprising 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories across eight distinct motion categories, alongside 10,109 simulation trajectories in the UAV-Flow-Sim environment equipped with task-specific completion criteria. Furthermore, we develop FlowVLA, which undergoes imitation pretraining on mixed real-sim demonstrations and online post-training via Tail-Aware GRPO (TGRPO). By leveraging group reward distributions, TGRPO effectively reinforces high-reward action sequences. Evaluated on 273 held-out UAV-Flow-Sim episodes, pretrained FlowVLA achieves a mean success rate of 75.58%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.72 percentage points, which TGRPO post-training further elevates to 93.16% with superior sample efficiency. Physical UAV experiments demonstrate robust execution of object-relative commands in both indoor and outdoor real-world scenes. Together, Flow establishes a novel benchmark and learning framework for language-conditioned flight maneuvers.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: ManiLadder: Benchmarking Robot Manipulation Through a Categorized and Multi-Difficulty Level Task Ladder
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Chongkai Gao, Jieao Shi, Zhaoyu Mu, Yudi Lin, Xuanwei Liu
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: ManiLadder introduces a structured benchmark with 112 robotic manipulation tasks across four difficulty levels, enabling systematic evaluation and comparison of learning progress in robotics.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Recent advances in robotic manipulation have enabled increasingly complex and dexterous behaviors, yet existing benchmarks still focus on simple pick-and-place tasks and lack a systematic framework for measuring progress in robot learning along the axis of task difficulty. We present ManiLadder, a large-scale and organized simulation benchmark for robotic manipulation. ManiLadder contains 112 carefully designed tasks stratified into 4 difficulty levels, with 8 categories in each level, spanning rigid-body and deformable-object manipulation, single-arm and dual-arm settings, and gripper and dexterous-hand end-effectors. To calibrate difficulty, we fix the data amount the same for every task and use a unified flow- matching imitation learning policy under the same training and evaluation protocols, then use its evaluation success rate as an operational empirical difficulty signal. All tasks are iteratively refined until they fall into target difficulty ranges, which are then verified across different random seeds, policies, and agentic learning systems. We further analyze the task properties, compare different policy performances and training settings, analyze task transfer and data scaling behaviors, and conduct real-world experiments showing that the designed tasks preserve their difficulty ordering beyond simulation. ManiLad- der provides a calibrated ladder for measuring, comparing, and advancing robotic manipulation capabilities. More results are available at https://maniladder-benchmark.github.io/.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Pengcheng Zhou, Xuanyu Liu, Yanchen Yin, Tianjie Ju, Bobo Li
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: LiveGeo introduces a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in dynamic geographic environments, revealing challenges in decision-making and evidence validation amid evolving contexts.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: We introduce GeoWorld, a controllable and continuously evolving geographic environment platform for LLM agents, and LiveGeo, a benchmark for evaluating reliable decision-making in real-world geographic environments using GeoWorld. Unlike existing evaluations that largely reason and plan over fixed geographic states, GeoWorld is grounded in real-world geographic structure and allows external world states to evolve along their own temporal processes while preserving verifiable state histories. LiveGeo places geographic tasks within this evolving environment, requiring agents to actively acquire task-relevant information, verify whether the evidence supporting prior decisions remains valid, and revise their plans when necessary. Our results reveal that even frontier LLMs struggle with static tasks, with no model consistently excelling across tasks, while strong static performance does not ensure dynamic reliability. Further analysis identifies a key bottleneck: agents struggle to acquire and translate relevant evidence into valid decisions and maintain their correctness as the world evolves. By releasing LiveGeo together with its GeoWorld platform, we aim to provide the community with a flexible and extensible infrastructure for studying the next generation of agents capable of reliable action in evolving geographic worlds.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: VOKE: Visual Object Kinematics Estimator for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Shengjia Zhu, Wenqiang Xu, Lin Shao
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: VOKE is a kinematics-aware perception framework that enhances object pose estimation and dynamics prediction for improved dexterous in-hand manipulation in robotics.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Vision-based dexterous in-hand manipulation requires knowing not only where an object is, but also how it moves. However, most robotic manipulation systems rely on off-the-shelf visual perception models whose outputs are limited to static object masks, geometry, or 6D poses, leaving downstream controllers to infer object dynamics implicitly from noisy visual observations. We present VOKE, a kinematics-aware perception framework that augments existing object and hand-object pose estimators to recover a complete object kinematic state comprising pose, linear and angular velocity, and linear and angular acceleration. VOKE contains two core perception modules and a downstream application study. First, a Pluggable Kinematics Module (PKM) attaches to the output of a standard pose estimator and predicts the object's linear and angular velocity and acceleration from temporal visual features. Second, a Kinematics-guided Pose Refinement Module (KPRM) converts this motion vector into a second-order, motion-prior reference pose and refines the per-frame pose estimates. We evaluate VOKE on DexYCB and OakInk, where it consistently improves object pose estimation across three different backbones and substantially reduces velocity and acceleration estimation error compared with pose differencing. As a downstream application, we use Kinematics-Augmented Reinforcement Learning (KARL) to compare a kinematics-augmented policy with a pose-history baseline. After training the policies in simulation, we transfer the kinematics-augmented policy to the physical robot without policy fine-tuning, demonstrating the complete perception-to-control pathway in the target domain.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: Quang Qui-Vinh Nguyen, Hung Nguyen, Rang Nguyen, Khoi Nguyen
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: This paper presents a training-free framework for Personalized Image Segmentation that improves instance discrimination in realistic scenes, outperforming existing methods while maintaining efficiency.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: \textbf{Personalized Image Segmentation (PIS)} aims to segment the specific object in a target image that matches a user-provided reference. Unlike category-based segmentation or few-shot segmentation, PIS must discriminate between multiple visually similar instances, a requirement central to deployed applications such as augmented reality, personalized content editing, robotics manipulation, inventory tracking, and fine-grained visual retrieval. We show that the strong numbers reported by existing PIS methods are largely an artifact of single-instance benchmarks: when evaluated on realistic scenes with several same-category look-alikes, prior point-prompt methods collapse, because the correct instance is frequently never surfaced as a prompt. We trace this to a recall bottleneck rather than a mask-quality one, and address it with a training-free, modular system. The pipeline first generates high-recall object proposals using an off-the-shelf class-agnostic detector, then matches each proposal to the reference using foundation-model features (e.g., BLIP-2), and finally refines the selected box with SAM. For robust matching we propose \textbf{top-$K$ Sinkhorn}, a patch-level distance that scores each candidate only on its most confidently matched patches; trimming the Sinkhorn dual potentials recovers the robustness of partial optimal transport at more than $100\times$ lower cost, keeping it inside the per-proposal candidate loop. To evaluate this regime, we introduce \textbf{\datasetname}, a realistic multi-instance benchmark. Across \datasetname, PerSeg, PerMIS, and DAVIS, our system surpasses PerSAM, $\mathrm{P}^2\mathrm{SAM}$, and PDM by up to $\sim\!48$ mIoU while matching their runtime and using fewer parameters, establishing a strong, deployable training-free baseline for real-world personalized segmentation.

Advanced Robotics Centre.title: ILA: A Transferable Interface-Level Adapter for Compliant Humanoid Motion Tracking
Advanced Robotics Centre.authors_text: ZhuoChang Cai, Zihao Yan, Jinxuan Zhu, Yanjie Li, Hao Xiong
Advanced Robotics Centre.summary: ILA is a sensor-free adapter that enhances compliant humanoid motion tracking by allowing robots to adapt to physical guidance without retraining existing motion trackers.
Advanced Robotics Centre.debug_abstract: Humanoid motion tracking is fundamental to reproducing human motions on humanoid robots and serves as an important tool for teleoperation and motion data collection. However, directly tracking reference motions can be unsafe in constrained environments or during physical human--robot interaction, motivating the need for compliant motion tracking. We present ILA, an Interface-Level Adapter for compliant humanoid motion tracking without dedicated interaction sensors. ILA adapts motion references from the robot's observation history, allowing the robot to respond to physical guidance while preserving the capabilities of a pretrained motion tracker. As an interface-level module, ILA can be directly plugged into different pretrained motion trackers without retraining either the adapter or the tracking policies. ILA is trained entirely in simulation to predict reference corrections induced by physical interaction. We evaluate ILA with three humanoid motion trackers and achieve a 63.6--75.4% reduction in guidance-target error compared with their original policies. Matched simulation studies and hardware experiments further show that ILA improves responsiveness to human guidance while preserving nominal motion-tracking performance. These results demonstrate compliant guidance as a reusable, sensor-free extension to pretrained humanoid motion trackers.

中国科学技术大学.title: TextGaze: Prompting Gaze Target Estimation with Textual Scene Cues
中国科学技术大学.authors_text: Junhui She, Fei Wang, Kun Li, Yiqi Nie, Yuxin Liu
中国科学技术大学.summary: TextGaze introduces a unified architecture using a Large Vision-Language Model for improved gaze target estimation, balancing visual saliency and semantic guidance without extensive annotations.
中国科学技术大学.debug_abstract: Gaze target estimation aims to infer the position of a person's gaze within a scene. Within mainstream design logic, multi-branch methods require extra supervision and annotations, while streamlined designs prioritize low-level visual saliency over true gaze intent. The former leads to a high annotation burden and hinders domain transfer, whereas the latter causes misalignment between predicted attention and actual gaze targets. To address this issue, we propose TextGaze, a unified cross-modal architecture that leverages a Large Vision-Language Model (LVLM) as scalable semantic guidance to balance the two design paradigms. The model extracts visual features from a frozen encoder and utilizes an LVLM to obtain gaze-aligned textual cues. We design a transformer-based fusion module with hierarchical text supervision to preserve task semantics. Lightweight decoding heads enable the joint prediction of gaze heatmaps and in-/out-of-frame status. We evaluate our method on four mainstream datasets, and the results show competitive performance across key metrics with robust cross-dataset generalisation without extra fine-tuning. Overall, we provide a streamlined alternative to traditional designs and highlight the potential of LVLMs as accessible auxiliary guidance for gaze estimation.

中国科学技术大学.title: Hint-Informed Self-Distillation for Reasoning Segmentation
中国科学技术大学.authors_text: Kunze Jiang, Yuchen Wang, Kang Li, Qixing Zhang
中国科学技术大学.summary: Hint-Informed Self-Distillation (HISD) enhances reasoning segmentation by utilizing external hints for token-level credit assignment, improving segmentation metrics while significantly reducing valid reasoning spans.
中国科学技术大学.debug_abstract: Reasoning segmentation requires identifying the target referred to by a query among visually similar objects, yet trajectory-level rewards cannot directly indicate which tokens provide relevant visual evidence. We propose Hint-Informed Self-Distillation (HISD), which uses target-disambiguation evidence for token-level credit assignment. An external model generates Segment Hints offline from training images, queries, and ground-truth target annotations, organizing target identity, discriminative attributes, confusable objects, and anchoring paths. A hint-conditioned exponential moving average teacher scores the student's own trajectories, and HISD computes the teacher-to-student evidence ratio over a token support set to adjust only the magnitudes of positive group-relative advantages, leaving nonpositive advantages unchanged. This design encourages concise reasoning while retaining the information needed for target disambiguation, and the student requires neither hints nor a teacher at inference. Under a unified training protocol, HISD improves ReasonSeg test gIoU and cIoU over our reproduction of DPAD by 3.00 and 3.55 percentage points, respectively. Across the five evaluated splits of ReasonSeg and the RefCOCO family, HISD achieves higher segmentation metrics than this baseline and reduces the average token count of valid reasoning spans by 80.17 to 91.83 percent.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Adapting Monocular Depth Estimation in Novel Scenes through Disparity Refinement and Robot Ego-Motion
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Dimitrios Chatziparaschis, Georgios Georgakis, Adnan I. Ansar, Shehryar Khattak, Konstantinos Karydis
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: EM-ViT enhances monocular depth estimation in novel scenes by refining disparity and leveraging robot ego-motion for real-time adaptation and improved accuracy.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: The geometric understanding of a scene is a crucial component for safe and efficient robotic operations in novel and unstructured environments. The recent emergence of foundation models for Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) has provided an opportunity to enrich robotic perception capabilities with dense long-range depth predictions, replacing expensive onboard hardware (e.g., LiDARs and stereo cameras). However, these offline models are primarily trained on affine-invariant depth representations, and their generalization to novel scenes remains unclear. In this work we present EM-ViT, a monocular depth estimation model that learns to adapt online relative depth inputs from a foundation model prior to the metric scale with observations collected during robotic operations. Motivated by the stereo camera parameterization, our method decomposes depth prediction via dense disparity refinement to recover the scene's relative structure and an effective baseline scalar prediction to determine the missing metric scale. The learning process leverages sparse LiDAR points and, optionally, the robot's Ego-Motion (EM) to rapidly train a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT), while an internal gradient matching loss preserves the fine-grained semantic structure of the input disparity in real-time. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on publicly available sequences, such as KITTI, and show that our online learning pipeline can adapt to novel scenes faster and with higher accuracy than existing MDE foundation models. The code and supplementary materials will be publicly available at https://emvit-mde.github.io.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: SunnyParking: Multi-Shot Trajectory Generation and Motion State Awareness for Human-like Parking
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Jishu Miao, Han Chen, Jiankun Zhai, Qi Liu, Tsubasa Hirakawa
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: SunnyParking introduces a dual-branch E2E architecture for autonomous parking that enhances trajectory generation and motion state awareness, outperforming traditional methods in complex scenarios.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Autonomous parking fundamentally differs from on-road driving due to its frequent direction changes and complex maneuvering requirements. However, existing End-to-End (E2E) planning methods often simplify the parking task into a geometric path regression problem, neglecting explicit modeling of the vehicle's kinematic state. This "dimensionality deficiency" easily leads to physically infeasible trajectories and deviates from real human driving behavior, particularly at critical gear-shift points in multi-shot parking scenarios. In this paper, we propose SunnyParking, a novel dual-branch E2E architecture that achieves motion state awareness by jointly predicting spatial trajectories and discrete motion state sequences (e.g., forward/reverse). Additionally, we introduce a Fourier feature-based representation of target parking slots to overcome the resolution limitations of traditional bird's-eye view (BEV) approaches, enabling high-precision target interactions. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework generates more robust and human-like trajectories in complex multi-shot parking scenarios, while significantly improving gear-shift point localization accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. We open-source a new parking dataset of the CARLA simulator, specifically designed to evaluate full prediction capabilities under complex maneuvers.

机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.title: QVS-LIVO RiskMap: Health- and Information-Aware View Selection for Multi-Camera LIVO and Off-Road Risk Mapping
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.authors_text: Zihan Pan, Jinghan Wang, Hang Li, Feng Cheng, Tianchen Liu
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.summary: The QVS-LIVO RiskMap system enhances multi-camera Lidar-Vision Odometry by selectively processing reliable views for accurate off-road risk mapping, achieving significant error reduction and real-time performance.
机器人技术与系统国家重点实验室.debug_abstract: Multi-camera observations in off-road environments vary significantly in reliability, posing challenges when complementing degraded geometric constraints. Motivated by this, we propose Quality-aware View Selection Lidar-Vision Odometry Risk Mapping (QVS-LIVO RiskMap), which decouples visual processing for state estimation from that for semantic mapping. The front end evaluates camera observations through read-only pretracking on a shared lidar-inertial posterior, combining observation health with geometric complementarity. Channel health memory and switching hysteresis govern selection of at most one eligible view for direct photometric correction. The posterior is retained when no view is eligible or the correction fails acceptance. The mapping back end integrates semantic observations from all available views in a shared world grid. Vehicle-scale geometry constrains semantic risk corrections, while spatial and temporal evidence supports risk confirmation. The system also produces a local bird's-eye-view (BEV) risk map and a global 2.5D semantic-terrain risk map with obstacle instance voxels. On two field sequences, QVS-LIVO achieved horizontal root mean square errors of 0.910 m and 1.664 m. It reduced error by 43.3% relative to FAST-LIO2 on the degraded long-route sequence. Across 12 controlled camera-fault configurations involving dropout, black frames and 60 ms timestamp shifts, it maintained complete trajectories with errors of 1.54-2.23 m. When deployed onboard an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the system generates local and global maps at 9.94 Hz and 2.00 Hz, respectively, with a median local mapping latency of 32.4 ms. These runtime results demonstrate the real-time feasibility of selective visual state updates alongside multi-view semantic mapping under challenging off-road conditions. The code and related resources are available at: https://github.com/zihanPan-HIT/QVS-LIVO.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yichi Zhang, Bo Wang, Zhenghan Zhu, Yutong Han, Jiayin Zou
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: HEIR is a resource for studying human-robot interactions by integrating speech, gaze, and video data to enhance intent understanding and task execution in natural settings.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: For robots to assist, serve, and collaborate with humans, they must not only interpret human requests conveyed through language and multimodal intentional cues, but also execute long-horizon tasks that interleave navigation and manipulation. In this paper, we introduce HEIR, a resource for studying how to Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interaction. HEIR pairs human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, while each session preserves successive episodes, with each request fulfilled through multiple execution subtasks. The captured data, together with human-authored annotations, support the study of intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion within a unified interaction setting. To demonstrate the value of HEIR, we conduct extensive offline experiments to evaluate how models benefit from additional human-centric context across these tasks, together with real-robot experiments that assess execution task completion. HEIR thus provides a valuable resource for studying user-centric robot interaction in naturalistic household environments. Our demo and dataset are available online.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Visual Cipher Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Reasoning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Deyao Hong, Jiayi Jiang, Yuchun Chen, Yixuan Shi, Wenyi Li
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: Visual Cipher Bench introduces a benchmark of 40 visual puzzles to assess long-horizon visual reasoning in LLM agents, revealing significant challenges in rule discovery from images.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: While language-model agents excel at long-horizon coding and terminal tasks, this success relies on two conditions: explicit text specifications and immediate execution feedback. However, neither condition holds in real-world problems where critical information exists only in images, leaving it unclear whether long-horizon capability transfers from text to visual reasoning. In such visual settings, because rules and clues resist text transcription and lack test-case feedback, agents must repeatedly inspect images, simulate spatial transformations, and autonomously cross-check clues. Despite this challenge, existing evaluations fail to capture such capability: visual reasoning benchmarks largely reduce tasks to single-turn, short-chain question answering, whereas agent benchmarks focus on text-based environments or interactive states that permit trial-and-error. To bridge this gap, we introduce Visual Cipher Bench, a collection of 40 original visual puzzles across four categories: spatial manipulation and simulation, logical constraints and planning, rule induction, and knowledge-based decoding. Each puzzle provides only one to three black-and-white line drawings and a minimal submission instruction, requiring agents to discover the underlying solving mechanism entirely from the images. Across 29 reasoning-effort configurations of eight frontier models, even the strongest model, GPT-6 Astra (max), achieves only 26.7% accuracy, while five of the eight models score below 1%. Yet on a ten-task subset, providing a single non-spoiler mechanism hint boosts accuracy from 7.8% to 55.6%. This sharp contrast shows that the primary bottleneck of current agents lies not in executing multi-step plans, but in autonomously discovering rules from visual evidence. Visual Cipher Bench thus provides a rigorous benchmark for measuring long-horizon visual reasoning in agents.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: ActWorld-JEPA: Action-Conditioned JEPA World Models Meet Latent Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Ziying Song, Shengkai Zhang, Caiyan Jia, Lei Yang, Lin Liu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: ActWorld-JEPA integrates action-conditioned latent prediction with relational reranking for improved autonomous driving decision-making, achieving high performance on benchmark evaluations.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) enable future prediction in latent space without pixel reconstruction. However, latent predictive consistency alone does not establish the relative driving quality of candidate plans. We present ActWorld-JEPA, a joint-embedding formulation for candidate-based driving. Where Plan-Conditioned JEPA (PC-JEPA) uses global and step-wise trajectory intentions to guide recurrent latent prediction, then combines the predicted future with the current scene through gated cross-attention; Relational Residual Reranking ($R^3$) models agreement and discrepancy between plan and future representations under planning supervision, yielding bounded, gated residual corrections to the base planning scores. This formulation connects latent prediction to candidate selection using only observed context and proposed trajectories at inference. Benchmark-specific implementations report 94.1 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, with the final selector calibrated using aggregate NAVTEST feedback, and 91.6 and 42.7 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest and navhard, respectively. The nuScenes evaluation reports a mean $L_2$ error of 1.20 m and a predicted collision rate of 0.76% over 1--6 s. This work provides an effective path from JEPA's predictive representations to driving decisions informed by anticipated consequences.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Enduo Zhao, Fangzhou Li, Yujie Zhu, Sicheng Lu, Fang Chen
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper presents a closed-loop framework for autonomous laparoscope control that integrates surgical phase recognition with visual perception to enhance target visibility and task execution in minimally invasive surgery.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Benchmark and phantom experiments evaluate the framework in surgical phase recognition, target tracking under occlusion and entity overlap, and autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: A Tactile-Informed Bi-Level Framework with Complementary Motion-Contact Planning and Tracking for Robust Model-Based In-Hand Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Yongpeng Jiang, Mingrui Yu, Yi Ren, Xiang Li
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: This paper presents a bi-level framework integrating tactile feedback with model-based control for robust in-hand manipulation, enhancing accuracy and adaptability in real-world tasks.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: In dexterous in-hand manipulation, learning-based methods achieve strong task performance with increasing generalization to unseen objects. A complementary advantage of model-based methods, central to this work, is online adaptation to new task specifications without policy retraining, given suitable system models. However, due to the complexity of physical contacts and limited sensing modalities, existing model-based methods still struggle with modeling errors, even when using advanced contact models or optimization schemes, which limit their real-world applications. To advance the effectiveness and robustness of model-based contact-rich in-hand manipulation, this paper proposes a novel bi-level framework with tactile incorporation to mitigate these limitations. Specifically, at the high level, reference finger motions and contacts are jointly generated via contact-implicit model predictive control. The high-level module enables online reactive planning and disturbance recovery. At the low level, these references are concurrently tracked through a hand force-motion model and tactile feedback. The low-level module compensates for modeling errors and enhances manipulation robustness. The complementarity between the two levels is manifested in two dimensions: 1) subsystem decomposition, with a slow optimization-based planning layer and a fast tactile-reactive control layer; and 2) functional decomposition, combining task-level optimality with contact-level stability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing model-based methods in accuracy and robustness, while supporting online replanning during execution. Our method successfully completes a diverse set of challenging tasks in real-world environments, even under appreciable external disturbances and modeling uncertainties.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: EMS-Nav: Embodied Multi-Scale Navigation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zenghui Yang, Xinan Wang, Danyang Li, Zhe Xu, Zheng Yang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: EMS-Nav is a biologically inspired framework that enhances multi-scale navigation efficiency for industrial inspection robots by organizing perception and navigation around local regions, improving success rates and reducing computational costs.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Industrial inspection robots must reach work areas and specific equipment. These destinations span spatial scales from regions to objects, so robots must relate each target to its surroundings to interpret the task and determine where to go. Existing methods support multi-scale navigation through rich environment representations, but at substantial computational and storage cost. These costs limit deployment where wireless coverage is incomplete and robots must rely on onboard computation to keep navigating. We introduce EMS-Nav, a biologically inspired multi-scale navigation framework for online, on-device operation. Its core innovation is to organize perception, spatial understanding, and navigation around regions, making local spaces the basic units of both environmental understanding and computation. EMS-Nav groups objects and their relationships into functionally meaningful spaces and builds a hierarchy from local areas to the broader environment. This organization supports efficient map construction alongside the interpretation and execution of language goals at different scales. In multi-scale navigation experiments, EMS-Nav achieves the highest success rates across all four target categories: objects, rooms, regions, and specific instances. It outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary mapping and navigation methods, improving overall first-attempt success by 9.39 percentage points over the strongest baseline while reducing mapping overhead and language-model input size. Local deployment in real indoor environments further demonstrates its applicability to on-device embodied navigation. By establishing regions as the organizing basis for perception, spatial understanding, and language-guided action, EMS-Nav provides a system that combines multi-scale understanding with computational efficiency to support diverse language goals on resource-constrained robots.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: FlashMotion: Ultra-Fast Long-Term 3D Motion Generation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Kaixing Yang, Xulong Tang, Ronghui Li, Xiangyue Zhang, Ziqiao Peng
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: FlashMotion introduces a novel framework for ultra-fast, high-quality long-term 3D motion generation, optimizing efficiency and performance across various interactive applications.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: 3D human motion generation plays a crucial role in game development, extended reality (XR), digital humans, and embodied simulation. Beyond motion generation, practical pipelines include rigging, retargeting, and rendering, making ultra-fast long-term 3D motion generation without compromising quality valuable for real-time interactive applications. Despite promising progress, high-quality long-horizon motion generation under tight inference budgets remains challenging, owing to 2 coupled bottlenecks: (1) generative strategies that require many sampling steps for high-quality 3D motion generation and (2) model architectures with substantial per-step computational and memory costs for long sequences. We present FlashMotion, a co-designed framework for high-quality long-horizon 3D motion generation under a strict inference budget, covering text-to-motion, music-to-dance, and speech-to-gesture tasks. To enhance trajectory-level efficiency, we introduce a 3D motion-space MeanFlow formulation with kinematic and dynamic consistency constraints for few-step generation, together with an Adaptive Soft masking mechanism for temporally coherent motion editing. To improve per-step efficiency, we design a lightweight non-autoregressive BiMamba architecture with condition-guided state selection and AdaIN-based condition fusion mechanism, enhancing cross-modal alignment and generalization to longer motion sequences. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FlashMotion achieves overall state-of-the-art performance in both quality and efficiency across text-to-motion, speech-to-gesture, and music-to-dance generation. The project page is available at https://sun-happy-ykx.github.io/FlashMotion-Project/

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: FORGE: Force-Aware Multi-Granularity Control for Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Liangjun Xing, Ke Fan, Kailin Li, Bin Wang, Xiaojie Niu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: FORGE is a novel force-aware control system for humanoid robots that enables efficient loco-manipulation through multi-granularity command processing and minimal input requirements.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated locomotion, balance regulation, and manipulation under frequent contacts, making teleoperated demonstration collection difficult: a practical controller must simultaneously provide precision, stability, and contact awareness. We propose FORGE, a force-aware multi-granularity control system with a coarse-to-fine command space spanning velocity navigation, planar foot placement, wrist-pose tracking, and optional force-conditioning inputs. Policy training requires no full-body human motion trajectories or joint-angle references; deployment consumes only sparse bilateral wrist poses relative to the pelvis, coarse motion commands, and optional desired wrist-load inputs. For sustained contact, FORGE combines a momentum observer with a learned correction trained using simulator contact-force supervision. At deployment, it estimates low-frequency, wrist-equivalent interaction forces from proprioception and reconstructed low-level arm PD torques, without wrist force/torque sensors. A quasi-static virtual-target loop uses this estimate and an optional desired applied-force input to adapt the wrist target. A frozen locomotion prior and asymmetric residual actions stabilize manipulation-induced whole-body corrections. Experiments evaluate unified-control stability, task-space tracking, quasi-static wrist-equivalent force estimation, squeezing forces during sustained contact with a rigid box, and downstream diffusion-policy execution of a squat-and-lift task across payload conditions. Website: https://bb0928.github.io/forge/.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jiachun Jin, Zetong Zhou, Haonan Wang, Xiao Yang, Jun Zhu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: SALA enhances latent action models by aligning human and robot actions semantically using unpaired video descriptions, improving training efficiency and real-world robot task performance.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Haofeng Wang, Pengcheng Wen, Ruiqi Li, Yuhao Zhang, Tiange Zhang
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: PhysCapBench is a novel benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, evaluating annotation quality across diverse domains to enhance language supervision in physical AI applications.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: What Can a VLA Learn from the Agent That Calls It? Task-Level Experience Distillation for Embodied Navigation
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Jinze Tao, Yuxiao Han, Kangkang Dong, Yancong Wei, Xiaojun Zhu
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The H2E method distills navigation experiences from agents into a VLA model, improving its success rate from 35.0% to 44.9% in unseen episodes.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Navigation agents use a large language model (LLM) planner to call a vision-language-action (VLA) model. Each episode needs the LLM, adding cost and delay. We distill successful agent experience into the VLA instead of distilling the planner. The VLA then navigates alone at test time. Agent sessions are not VLA demonstrations. They include motions driven by planner tools and sub-instructions, along with detours. We present H2E, a task-level experience distillation method that converts these sessions into VLA training data. Every motion becomes a VLA action under the original task instruction, with the resulting poses as targets. H2E masks the loss on steps that move away from the goal. It labels every visited state within 1 m of the goal as a stop. We then update the VLA with low-rank adaptation. The VLA learns to stop at the goal and find goals the base model never reaches. On all 3,189 REVERIE-CE val-unseen episodes, H2E raises the success rate of an 8B VLA from 35.0% to 44.9%.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Zefan Wang, Yufan Dang, Xuanwei Shi, Mingqi Gao, Cheng Yin
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: JustRUA demonstrates that a simplified harness for GPT-6 Astra significantly enhances robot arm performance on RoboDojo, achieving a score increase from 29.7 to 50.3.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most. Even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning, this simple harness raises the score on the RoboDojo simulation benchmark substantially, from 29.7 to 50.3.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Chenhao Zhang, Hanyu Zhao, Zihan Que, Hang Cheng, Tengfei Pan
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: WISE introduces a framework for efficiently scheduling world-model imagination in post-training vision-language-action models, enhancing policy refinement and reducing computational costs while improving robustness.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Post-training VLA policies typically rely on supervised fine-tuning with costly expert demonstrations or reinforcement learning with expensive and potentially unstable real-world exploration. World models offer a promising alternative by evaluating candidate behaviors through imagined futures, yet effective post-training requires more than accurate prediction: imagination must be scheduled where it is useful, bounded within reliable horizons, and translated into trustworthy policy supervision. In robotic manipulation, the value of imagination varies substantially across execution stages, while extended rollouts can accumulate prediction errors and introduce unreliable learning signals. We introduce WISE (World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models), a unified framework that coordinates when and how world-model imagination is used during policy refinement. WISE selectively invokes imagination at interaction-relevant states, performs bounded multi-view rollouts, evaluates candidate futures using progress and completion signals, and uses their relative outcomes to refine actions generated from real interaction contexts. Extensive experiments with both $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$ demonstrate consistent improvements across diverse manipulation tasks while reducing GPU computation time by approximately 80% compared with full imagination. Real-world evaluations further show substantial gains in robustness and generalization under diverse real-world distribution shifts.

智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).title: Does Seeing More Mean Knowing More? Mono-Anchored Advantage Normalization for Multi-Source Visual Reasoning
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).authors_text: Fanhu Zeng, Zhicong Luo, Zefan Wang, You Li, Chi Chen
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).summary: The paper introduces MARS, a mono-anchored multi-source reasoning framework that improves visual reasoning by effectively integrating diverse information sources while minimizing interference, achieving notable performance gains.
智能系统与机器人实验室 (ISR Lab).debug_abstract: Visual reasoning through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has achieved remarkable progress. However, when dealing with multi-source inputs, existing approaches tend to treat them as a mere accumulation of information, lacking explicit mechanisms to distinguish whether integrating additional sources yields information gain or introduces interference. Therefore, they struggle to effectively model dynamic interaction when integrating multiple sources, particularly when they differ significantly in physical properties and semantics, e.g., infrared and depth, leading to inferior performance to mono-source reasoning when a certain source holds the dominant signal.
